description: EXP-A frozen corpus (roadmap work/roadmaps/agent-harness-capabilities/05-learning-and-evaluation.md L4) exercising the real runtime/context_builder.py::_select_skills selector through runtime/skills/evaluation.py::evaluate_skill_selection. Each case carries both a human-readable `task` description (for the SkillSelectionCorpus schema) and the literal `task_type`/`project_id`/`output_paths` fixture fields that `_select_skills` actually reads to derive its token signals -- the two are designed to agree, but only the fixture fields drive the real selector under test.

candidates.name: incident-response-playbook
candidates.description: Runbook for triaging active production incidents, assessing customer impact, coordinating rollback, and identifying root cause during an outage.

candidates.name: api-contract-review
candidates.description: Checklist for reviewing changes to a public HTTP API contract, including backward compatibility, versioning, and breaking-change detection.

candidates.name: secrets-rotation
candidates.description: Procedure for rotating leaked or expiring credentials, access keys, and certificates across services without downtime.

candidates.name: load-test-planning
candidates.description: Guide for designing and running load and performance tests against a service before a capacity-sensitive launch.

candidates.name: changelog-authoring
candidates.description: Guidance for writing a clear customer-facing changelog entry that summarizes a release's user-visible changes.

cases.task: A payment processor outage is in progress; investigate impact and start the incident timeline.
cases.note: task_type/project_id/path tokens overlap only with the incident-response-playbook description.

cases.task: Review the proposed billing API contract change for backward compatibility before merge.
Rotate the auth platform's leaked secrets immediately.
cases.note: project_id deliberately uses 'platform' rather than 'service' to avoid an accidental token collision with load-test-planning's description (which contains the singular token 'service').

cases.task: Plan a load test for the checkout service ahead of the holiday traffic spike.
Write the changelog entry for the next public release.
cases.note: project_id deliberately avoids the literal word 'public' to avoid an accidental token collision with api-contract-review's description.

cases.task: Our checkout flow just went down -- figure out the blast radius and get a postmortem started.
cases.note: Reworded prose describing the same intent as EXPA-001; the structured fixture fields (task_type=incident_response, project_id/path containing 'outage') still literally overlap with the Skill description, so the selector succeeds even though the free-text framing changed.

cases.task: Our identity platform's access keys are expiring; cycle them across every service with zero downtime.
cases.note: Genuine intent matches secrets-rotation, but every fixture token ('key' singular, 'cycling', 'identity', 'platform', 'refresh', 'tokens') is a synonym rather than a literal match for the Skill's description tokens ('rotation', 'rotating', 'credentials', 'keys' plural, 'certificates', ...). Documented as an expected miss: the selector only does literal any-token-overlap matching, so a genuine vocabulary shift with zero literal overlap is invisible to it.

cases.task: Write a marketing blog post recapping our Q3 product launches for the public site.
cases.note: Deliberately designed to expose the selector's permissiveness: task_type contributes the token 'writing', which also appears in changelog-authoring's description ('Guidance for writing a clear customer-facing changelog entry...'). A marketing blog post is not a changelog entry, so this is expected to be a genuine false activation on the real selector, not a corpus bug.

cases.task: Refresh the company logo and brand palette for the upcoming rebrand.
cases.note: Superficially adjacent to 'design'/'review' style Skill names but shares zero literal tokens with any candidate description; included as the abstain-side control case that the selector is expected to handle correctly, contrasting with EXPA-008.

cases.task: Clean up the vector math helper library; no behavior change intended.
cases.note: No candidate Skill covers general internal refactors; zero token overlap by design.

cases.task: Schedule the quarterly team offsite and draft the agenda.
cases.note: task_type deliberately says 'scheduling' rather than 'planning' to avoid an accidental token collision with load-test-planning's description (which contains the token 'planning').

cases.task: An incident is in progress because leaked secrets were used to access production; rotate the leaked credentials and write the incident report.
cases.note: Legitimately implicates two Skills at once: incident-response-playbook via incident/response/outage tokens, secrets-rotation via secrets/leaked tokens.
